clue.text: Each favoured supporter embraces United constantly

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within, so the string built from the first words takes another letter inside it

parts.note: per means each, as in 'a pound per head'
a pet is a favoured one, as in teacher's pet
an ally is a supporter
U is the usual abbreviation for United in team names

explanation.surface: A loyal backer of every match keeps hugging Manchester United, season after season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraces' acts on the whole run of the first three pieces, not just 'supporter', so the U lands in the middle of the string.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done perpetually happens without ceasing, which is what constantly means.

clue.text: Banished sweetheart glib about kiss

indicators.note: about means around, so the first pair of pieces goes round the kiss

parts.note: the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E
a pat answer is a glib one
X is the conventional kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A lover is sent away for a smooth-tongued attitude to kissing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' is not a lover but the heart of 'sweet', its middle letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: An expatriate lives outside their own country, and one exiled from home is said to be banished.

clue.text: Plain couple that is accepting resistance

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the string from the couple and 'that is' takes another letter inside

parts.note: a couple is a pair
R is the symbol for resistance in physics
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A plain-speaking couple, that is, will tolerate some opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts R inside PAIRIE, right after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a wide, flat, grassy expanse, a kind of plain, as in North America.

clue.text: Sailor going over fathom mark

indicators.note: in a down clue, the sailor goes over, above, the next piece

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
to fathom is to understand, to get it

explanation.surface: A sailor sounds the depth, crossing a fathom marker on the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fathom' looks like a nautical depth beside the sailor, but here it is the verb meaning understand.
explanation.definitionFit: A target is something aimed at, a mark in the sense of an object of aim.

clue.text: Article on coins absorbing single seniors

indicators.note: in a down clue, the article sits on top of the rest

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the coins take the single inside

parts.note: cents are small coins
I is the Roman numeral one, a single

explanation.surface: An item about coinage soaking up a lone pensioner's savings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbing' puts I inside CENTS to make CEINTS.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancients are the elders, people of great age, a playful match for seniors.

clue.text: Lethargy of Left facing irritation, say

indicators.note: say tells you the letters built are only how the answer sounds when spoken

parts.note: L for left, set facing (in front of) ANGER for irritation, gives LANGER

explanation.surface: A sluggish politician on the left facing public irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: L plus ANGER gives LANGER, which in a non-rhotic British accent is said just like the answer; 'say' signals that sound match.
explanation.definitionFit: Languor is a dreamy lack of energy or spirit, the same idea as lethargy.

clue.text: Display stamina with fit one running

indicators.note: running as in running wild or running loose suggests the letters are scattered and reformed

explanation.surface: A fit person shows their stamina while out running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' fits the athletic picture but is the anagram signal for STAMINA, FIT and ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifestation is an outward showing of something, a display of it.

clue.text: Detective heading tough precinct

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading means going at the top of the next piece

parts.note: DI is Detective Inspector
strict means tough, unbending

explanation.surface: A detective in charge of a hard-bitten police precinct.
explanation.definitionFit: A district is an area marked off for administration, like a precinct of a city.

clue.text: Wandering on pier, tearing around

indicators.note: around means turned about or reordered, so these letters are put in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone ambles along a pier, then dashes about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tearing around' reads as one phrase, but 'tearing' is part of the fodder and 'around' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A peregrination is a long journey or meander, travelling from place to place.

clue.text: First Letter to the Corinthians?

parts.note: Paul's epistle is the Bible's First Letter to the Corinthians; read literally, the opening character of the script the people of Corinth wrote in

explanation.surface: A reference to St Paul's first epistle to the church at Corinth.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bible book is a red herring: Corinth was Greek, so the first letter they wrote with was the start of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek alphabet opens with this character, so it is literally the Greeks' first letter.

clue.text: Bury the hatchet relic once repaired

indicators.note: something repaired has been put back together, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Making peace once an old relic has been mended.
explanation.definitionFit: To bury the hatchet is an idiom for making peace after a quarrel, settling differences.

clue.text: Get involved with some painter, Venetian?

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Taking part alongside some artist from Venice, perhaps Titian.
explanation.definitionFit: To intervene is to step into a situation, to get involved in it.

clue.text: Loose woman who's related going topless

indicators.note: topless means losing the top, the first letter of the word

parts.note: an auntie is a female relative

explanation.surface: A wanton female relative strips off her top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose' is not an adjective about the woman but a verb, set free. 'going topless' drops the A from AUNTIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To loose a knot or a rope is to undo it, to set it free.

clue.text: Avoid oddly easy bite

indicators.note: oddly means taking the odd-numbered letters, first and third, of the word

parts.note: to bite food is to chew it

explanation.surface: Steer clear of a strangely easy mouthful.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew something is to shun it on purpose, deliberately keep away from it.

clue.text: Bewildered criminal stopped working?

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
an appliance that has fused has blown its fuse and stopped working

explanation.surface: A baffled crook asks whether he has stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone confused is puzzled and lost, unable to make sense of things, which is bewildered.

clue.text: More resolute learner comprehending arithmetic?

indicators.note: comprehending means taking in or including, so the learner holds the letter

parts.note: a studier is one who studies, a learner
arithmetic is one of the three Rs, so it gives R

explanation.surface: A more determined student finally grasping arithmetic.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic, are the basics of schooling, so any one of them can give R.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturdier means stronger and firmer, and figuratively more resolute and unshakeable.

clue.text: Drug source keeps English detectives up

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the source holds the next pieces

parts.note: a mine is a source, as in a mine of information

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detectives

explanation.surface: An informant about drugs keeps English police detectives in the loop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses only the detectives; 'keeps' then holds the English letter and the reversal together.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicine is a drug used to treat illness.

clue.text: Barrel with good gun metal

parts.note: a tun is a large barrel or cask
the Sten is a British submachine gun of the Second World War

explanation.surface: A barrel with a decent gun-metal finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tungsten is a hard grey metallic element used in light-bulb filaments.

clue.text: Singer thus performed in elevated work

parts.note: so means thus, in this way

indicators.note: in places the performed piece inside the work
in a down clue, elevated means raised, read upwards and so backwards

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
ran means operated, performed, as a machine runs

explanation.surface: A singer has performed in a lofty piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' reads as lofty, praising the work, but in a down clue it turns the work upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano is a singer with the highest female or boy's voice.

clue.text: Almost grill French dish

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of it, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a grating is a grill of bars

explanation.surface: A French dish nearly ready to go under the grill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grill' looks like the cooking method, but it is a grating of metal bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A gratin is a French dish topped with browned breadcrumbs or cheese.

clue.text: Fuming Queen upset European ruler

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the conventional Queen
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: An angry queen is upset by a European monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fuming' looks like anger, but it is meant literally: giving off smoke or a smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeking means giving off a strong smell or smoke, as something fuming does.

clue.text: Main Church holding new spiritualist meeting

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the sea and church together hold the next letter

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open sea
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The principal church hosts a fresh gathering of spiritualists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like an adjective, chief, but it is the noun, the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A seance is a gathering where people try to contact the spirits of the dead.

clue.text: President beginning to touch bottom

indicators.note: beginning to means take the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the rump is the hindquarters, the bottom

explanation.surface: A president starts to touch rock bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald Trump served as President of the United States.

clue.text: Awkward cut from fine leg anticipated

indicators.note: cut from says the letters are sliced out of the words that follow, running across them

explanation.surface: A cricketer fielding at fine leg is clumsy, as expected.
explanation.walkthrough: Fine leg is a cricket fielding position behind the batsman on the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelegant means lacking grace, which is what awkward also means.

clue.text: A tax raised for Budget

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means lifted up, read backwards from bottom to top

parts.note: a toll is a charge or tax, as on a road or bridge

explanation.surface: A tax rise announced in the Budget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Budget' looks like the Chancellor's annual statement, but it is the verb, to apportion.
explanation.definitionFit: To budget an amount is to set it aside for a purpose, to allot it.

clue.text: Campaign speech includes empty platitude

indicators.note: includes means holds inside, so the speech holds the next letters

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

indicators.note: empty means with the inside removed, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: An electioneering speech packed with hollow clichés.
explanation.definitionFit: An operation is an organised military action, a campaign in the army's sense.

clue.text: One grand lavatory for cool house

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
G is short for a grand, a thousand pounds
loo is British slang for a lavatory

explanation.surface: A single fancy toilet for a trendy house.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is a dome-shaped Inuit dwelling built of snow, a house that is literally cold.

clue.text: Governs, yet somehow keeps current autonomy

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the jumbled letters hold the next one
somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: A government still somehow holds on to the present self-rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' puts I inside the rearranged letters of GOVERNS YET.
explanation.definitionFit: Sovereignty is a state's supreme power over itself, its independence or self-government.
